title: Frank Pena, the Dew Drop and acts on the road
summary: He recalls Frank Pena, stranded bands, Joe Anderson's arrangements, Ray Charles living nearby, and drummer Lil June.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Did you know Frank Pannier very well?
Oh yeah, he was a nice guy, man. I knew his wife. I knew his sons and daughter. Yeah.
Was that like working for a family when you worked for them?

Well, they never were actually in there. Frank did all the business with everybody because everybody come there, a lot of times bands would get stranded at his place. And he'd make them play music for them living there. Yeah. In fact, Joe Anderson came with his band. He was from Carolina. And he came there, he got stranded with his band so we were able to get a few arrangements from his band to go with Lloyd's band, which was really nice, man. Ray Charles used to live down the street at the club on the Fosters. He used to live there. He'd walk so many steps to get into the place, he knew exactly where to go. And Charles Brown, Jimmy Witherspoon, man, I've been on stage with a lot of people at the Dewdrop. A lot of people there. But we had a little drummer, man. A little guy, he's from Atlanta. He came there with this girl, she could dance. He got hooked up with a band. He went to some part of Texas and boy got hooked up with the wrong stuff and died in Texas. He was a hell of a drummer. He had something for you. If you walk, he had something for you on the drums. Anything you did, and when that girl danced, he had something for her. And he really made her really shine. Because most of the drummers, you know, you'd be playing, you know, some kind of rhythm like that. But he had something different for her than most drummers. And everybody in town would come to hear Lil' June play. I didn't know his last name, but they just called him Lil' June. Lil' June? Yeah. Lil' June? Yeah. Lil' June? Yeah. J-U-N-E? J-U-N-E? Yeah, J-U-N-E, yes. He's from Atlanta. He came down there with Chuck Willis. Chuck Willis' man came there. We ran into all kind of people on the road, man. You never know who you're going to play with. At no time did you know. When we went to the Polytheatre, let me see, Charlie Barnett's band was featured. Phyllis Branch, she graduated from Xavier University. Yeah. And then, yeah, we got to the Polytheatre. And then, yeah, we got to the Polytheatre. And then, yeah, we got to the Polytheatre. And then, yeah, we got to the Polytheatre. And then, yeah, Branch, she sang at, she graduated from Xavier University. This other group, his group, they were on the same show with us. Bonnie Briggs at Tap Dance, he was on that show. Now, we were supposed to, when Slim finished his act, his last song, he was supposed to stop playing, the band, we were playing in B-flat, and then the band was supposed to modulate to D-flat.
